survivors.claim: The new attrValuesOf helper scans the raw document rather than matched tags, so D3's inline style= sweep now fires on text that is not an attribute at all - visible screen copy containing 'style =' and a style= attribute inside an HTML comment both produce an inline-style violation. It is also the only function in wire-register.js that does not run the module's own stripComments() first, breaking the invariant the module header states ('HTML comments are stripped first') and that its owner spec recorded a defect for ('a wireframe whose gray links survived only in a comment read as drawn').
survivors.impact: A screen whose own words happen to contain that one word followed by an equals sign, or that keeps a commented-out fragment, fails the gate for a style it does not have.
survivors.evidence:
Executed against the shipped tree. Prose case: synthetic host, approved wire-linking mock whose only body is '

Pick a font style = serif or sans

' -> 'design/mocks/x.html: 1 inline style= attribute(s)', exit 1. The pre-fix regex required a quote and did not match this, so the false positive is new in this delta. Comment case: attrValuesOf('','style') -> ["a"], where stylesheetTargets on the same input returns [] because it strips comments first.

survivors.claim: wire-register.js's header usage line still names only two of its three exports after attrValuesOf was added, so the file's mandated header no longer names its own public surface. The file is also out of the spec's File Plan (recorded in the deviations sidecar).
survivors.impact: The one place a reader looks to learn what this shared module offers omits its newest function.
survivors.evidence: Worker Rules: 'Every script starts with a header comment: usage line, the one owner citation ... what it deliberately does NOT do'. Line 1 lists two of three exports; the export statement lists three. Executed: scope-reconcile --json -> outOfPlan: ["spec/scripts/lib/wire-register.js"]. On merits the placement is right - purely additive, no existing function altered, all four existing call sites untouched, and it avoids a third hand-rolled attribute parser which is the exact divergence this module's owner spec exists to prevent - so the residue is header currency only.
